categoryNotes.chatAgent: F110 S3 (docs/research/2026-07-28-legacy-retirement.md, this feature's largest category): went 122 -> 9 by patching both reachability paths (missing-services.js's import/class/registerSingleton three-part registration and services.js's export re-export line) for 89 tokens covering the chat/inlineChat/agentHost/agentEditorComments trees, plus two directory segments this slice found were genuinely AI/Agent debt but had never been covered by any of the 12 category matchers (platform/agentPlugins/**, a real Claude/Copilot/OpenPlugin-format AI agent plugin manifest and hook parser, not a stub -- and workbench/contrib/agentsVoice/**, an AI voice-agent stub pair), plus one filename-based special case (networkFilterService.service.js, matched like authAccount's globalCompositeBar.js by filename rather than directory shape). mcp's last remaining file (mcpPlatformTypes.js) fell out to 0 as a side effect: its only consumer was agentHostCustomizationService.service.js, one of the 122 chatAgent debt sources this slice removed. The 9 that remain are NOT missing-services.js stub noise -- a dependency-graph audit restricted to the real, currently bundled 2057-source corpus (not a static grep over the whole vendor tree, which is dominated by files that never actually reach the real bundle) found each is kept alive by a real, always-instantiated Plain feature with a non-optional constructor dependency, or by a real, non-DI content import: (1) chat/browser/chat.service.js -- IChatWidgetService is a non-optional __param of THREE real Quick Access providers this slice found: AnythingQuickAccessProvider (Go to Anything), GotoSymbolQuickAccessProvider (Go to Symbol in File) and SymbolsQuickAccessProvider (Go to Symbol in Workspace); IQuickChatService/IChatAccessibilityService/IChatCodeBlockContextProviderService share the same import line and file, so all four registrations are kept as a group (removing three of four buys nothing -- the file stays regardless). (2) chat/common/participants/chatAgents.service.js -- IChatAgentService is a non-optional __param of @codingame/monaco-vscode-quickaccess-service-override's CommandsQuickAccessProvider, i.e. the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) itself; IChatAgentNameService shares the same import line and stays alongside it. (3) chat/browser/actions/chatConstants.js and (4) chat/common/constants.js -- both real, non-optional content imports of CommandsQuickAccessProvider (ASK_QUICK_QUESTION_ACTION_ID/CHAT_OPEN_ACTION_ID from the former, ChatAgentLocation from the latter) -- a second override package (quickaccess-service-override) this slice's initial package-level sweep had not inspected, discovered only by real-content grep after the string ASK_QUICK_QUESTION_ACTION_ID failed to disappear from a real rebuild despite removing every known reachability path inside @codingame/monaco-vscode-api itself. (5) chat/common/chatSessionsService.js and (6) chatSessionsService.service.js, (7) chat/common/model/chatUri.js, and (8) services/chat/common/chatEntitlementService.js (the real impl class, not the .service.js token file -- kept for its ChatEntitlementContextKeys export) -- all four are transitively imported by chat/common/constants.js, so they collapse into the same Command Palette dependency chain as (4). (9) platform/networkFilter/common/networkFilterService.service.js -- IAgentNetworkFilterService is a non-optional __param of browserView.js's real BrowserViewModel ("Share with Agent" + Playwright-based agent browser-observation bridge); untangling it requires refactoring BrowserViewModel's tracked-sharing-state machinery (IPlaywrightService alone is threaded through five separate call sites in that class), a materially deeper surgery than a dependency-line removal -- flagged as a follow-up candidate, not attempted in this slice. Two additional real, non-chat consumers were also found and neutralized without leaving a floor: editorAccessibilityHelp.js's getChatCommandInfo/getChatEditInfo (real accessibility-help content, gated behind ChatContextKeys/ctxHasEditorModification/ctxHasRequestInProgress that always evaluate false now that chat is gone) were simplified in-place to always return nothing, which let chat/common/actions/chatContextKeys.js and chat/browser/chatEditing/chatEditingEditorContextKeys.js drop out entirely; inlineCompletionLanguageStatusBarContribution.js (a Copilot-branded "$(copilot) Inline completion available" status bar item gated behind IChatEntitlementService#sentimentObs) was reduced to a no-op registration, which let IChatEntitlementService's own registration in missing-services.js be removed safely. Expected floor after any future slice that takes on the extensionRuntime/BrowserViewModel surgery: 8 (everything except networkFilterService.service.js).

categoryNotes.authAccount:
F110 S2 removed the import/class/registerSingleton three-part registration for 8 of the 9 non-globalCompositeBar authAccount tokens from missing-services.js (IAuthenticationAccessService, IAuthenticationMcpAccessService, IAuthenticationMcpService, IAuthenticationMcpUsageService, IAuthenticationUsageService, IAuthenticationExtensionsService, IAuthenticationQueryService, IDynamicAuthenticationProviderStorageService), plus the matching services.js re-export lines. Verified by real rebuild: authAccount went 11 -> 5, not the naively-predicted 1 — a real dependency sweep (grepping every real, currently-bundled file for each token, not just the 13 override packages) found that globalCompositeBar.js (kept then; migrated in F110 S4, see below) has three of its own direct, real import-time dependencies into the authentication/** tree, entirely independent of missing-services.js: (a) common/authentication.js for the INTERNAL_AUTH_PROVIDER_PREFIX constant; (b) common/authentication.service.js for the IAuthenticationService decorator token itself, injected as globalCompositeBar.js's own non-optional constructor dependency (AccountsActivityActionViewItem/SimpleAccountActivityActionViewItem) — this is also why missing-services.js's IAuthenticationService registerSingleton was the one registration S2 deliberately did NOT remove, unlike every other authAccount/mcp/syncEditSessions token: removing it would have left the token unbound and thrown at Activity Bar construction time, the same 'constructor-required DI dependency' trap F080 S2 hit with IChatEditingService; (c) browser/authenticationService.js for the getCurrentAuthenticationSessionInfo function — and that file's own (never-instantiated, but still present) AuthenticationService class in turn imports browser/authenticationAccessService.service.js, which real rebuild confirmed stays reachable through that chain even though nothing requires IAuthenticationAccessService's DI binding itself. F110 S2's predicted floor was 5: globalCompositeBar.js + these 4 files, expected to zero out once F110 S4 migrated globalCompositeBar.js into app/. F110 S4's first pass did exactly that migration (activitybarPart.js's sole GlobalCompositeBar construction site now imports PlainGlobalCompositeBar/PlainGlobalActivityActionViewItem from app/features/workbench/plain-global-composite-bar.ts instead, and missing-services.js's IAuthenticationService import/class/registerSingleton triple — the one token S2 could not remove — is now fully deleted, verified by grep: zero remaining references) — but a real rebuild found authAccount stayed at 5, NOT the planned 0. Root cause, found only by real dependency-graph investigation after the ratchet didn't move: activitybarPart.js was never globalCompositeBar.js's only consumer. @codingame/monaco-vscode-view-title-bar-service-override's titlebarPart.js (a real, currently-reachable file — Plain's custom title bar, confirmed present in the dist source map with layout.contribution.darwin/win/linux) independently imports four names directly from '@codingame/monaco-vscode-api/vscode/vs/workbench/browser/parts/globalCompositeBar': SimpleGlobalActivityActionViewItem (real and reachable — renders the same Manage gear inside the title bar/Command Center layout, gated on action.id === GLOBAL_ACTIVITY_ID with no dead condition guarding it) plus SimpleAccountActivityActionViewItem/isAccountsActionVisible/AccountsActivityActionViewItem (confirmed dead — grepping the real, currently-bundled @codingame packages found ACCOUNTS_ACTIVITY_ID is never used to register any action anywhere, so titlebarPart.js's own action.id === ACCOUNTS_ACTIVITY_ID branch never fires, mirroring globalCompositeBar.js's own already-dead account branch). This second consumer was missed by every earlier sweep (F110 S2's categoryNotes and this migrated file's own doc comment both claimed 'sole consumer'/'no consumer at all' for these exports, based on greps that evidently did not reach across every installed @codingame override package). Confirmed by a controlled before/after rebuild diff (reverting only the patch/lockfile, rebuilding, diffing the full source lists): the ONLY source-map change from that first pass was one net-new source, app/features/workbench/plain-global-composite-bar.ts (2057 -> 2058) — zero vendor files, including all 5 authAccount debt sources, dropped out.

F110 S4's second pass closed this gap: patches/@codingame__monaco-vscode-view-title-bar-service-override@35.0.1.patch (the first-ever patch of this transitive-only package, pulled in by @codingame/monaco-vscode-workbench-service-override, which Plain does depend on directly) repoints titlebarPart.js's SimpleGlobalActivityActionViewItem import at this repo's own PlainSimpleGlobalActivityActionViewItem (app/features/workbench/plain-global-composite-bar.ts, a second port alongside PlainGlobalCompositeBar/PlainGlobalActivityActionViewItem, reusing the same DI-registration discipline), deletes the two branches that only ever served the already-dead account UI (the ACCOUNTS_ACTIVITY_ID SimpleAccountActivityActionViewItem construction, and the isAccountsActionVisible(...) guard — that helper is vendor code already neutered to always return false by the untouched globalCompositeBar.js hunk, so the guarded push was already unreachable regardless), and inlines AccountsActivityActionViewItem.ACCOUNTS_VISIBILITY_PREFERENCE_KEY's literal string value ("workbench.activity.showAccounts") so the last reference to that class's import could drop too. A real rebuild (controlled before/after diff, reverting only this new patch and rebuilding both ways) confirmed exactly 5 real files disappeared from the bundle and 0 were added: globalCompositeBar.js, authenticationAccessService.service.js, authenticationService.js and authentication.js (4 of the 5 catalogued authAccount debt sources) plus base/common/oauth.js — a genuinely new, previously-uncatalogued source that turned out to be reachable only through authenticationService.js/authentication.js's own import chain and was never itself classified into any of the 12 debt categories (its path is base/common/oauth.js, matching neither the /authentication|accounts?/ segment regex nor the defaultAccount.js/globalCompositeBar.js filename special case), so it is not listed as a debtSources entry here — it simply no longer appears anywhere in the real dist output.

authAccount reached 1, not 0: authentication.service.js itself remains reachable through a third, independent real consumer this slice's brief did not anticipate — @codingame/monaco-vscode-api's own workbench/services/chat/common/chatEntitlementService.js (already one of the 9 catalogued chatAgent debt sources, kept alive by chat/common/constants.js's Command Palette import chain, per chatAgent's own categoryNotes point 8). That file's ChatEntitlementRequests class takes IAuthenticationService as a non-optional __param (line ~829 of the real installed file), and its own top-level `import { IAuthenticationService } from '../../authentication/common/authentication.service.js'` line statically pulls authentication.service.js into the bundle the moment chatEntitlementService.js is loaded — completely independent of globalCompositeBar.js/titlebarPart.js, and undetectable by this slice's grep-the-vendor-tree method alone (chatEntitlementService.js was already known-and-accepted chatAgent debt; nobody had reason to re-audit its own import list for authAccount-relevant tokens until the ratchet on this specific category stopped moving). Real content inspection confirms this is inert at runtime, not a live risk: IChatEntitlementService's own registerSingleton registration was removed from missing-services.js back in F110 S3, so nothing in the running app ever asks the DI container to construct ChatEntitlementService (the only class whose constructor could reach ChatEntitlementRequests, itself only built lazily off a this.requests Lazy wrapper that is never forced) — the exact same 'real class in a real, reachable file, but never actually instantiated because its own DI registration was removed' pattern already established for AccountsActivityActionViewItem before this slice, just one level further down the same file's dependency graph. Per the main session's own standing instruction for this slice (do not invent a fourth vendor-package patch or a different architecture to force a floor of exactly 0), this one remaining file was left alone rather than adding a fifth, unplanned hunk to chatEntitlementService.js — categoryCeilings.authAccount is set to the real, honestly-measured floor of 1, and debtSources below lists only authentication.service.js. A future slice could close this true final gap by inlining IAuthenticationService's own decorator-token value as a plain string constant directly in chatEntitlementService.js (mirroring this slice's own ACCOUNTS_VISIBILITY_PREFERENCE_KEY inlining technique) or by auditing whether ChatEntitlementRequests' IAuthenticationService parameter can be dropped outright — neither was attempted here, as it falls outside F110 S4's authorized scope (the Activity Bar/title-bar Manage gear migration only).

note: F110 S0 (docs/research/2026-07-28-legacy-retirement.md, decision points 4/5): this baseline is a ratchet, not a fixed value. scripts/plain/check-bundle.mjs fails a category only when its real debt-source count exceeds categoryCeilings[category], or when it contains a source path never catalogued in debtSources for that category before -- either signals a regression. A category shrinking (fewer or zero real members, all already present in debtSources) passes without editing this file; that is deliberate, so later F110 cleanup slices are never tempted to mask a regression by hand-editing a number. debtSources is the explicit, machine-generated floor list acceptance #5's own research called for ("哪些文件还在、各自为什么还在") -- see categoryNotes per category for why each group is still present and when it is expected to reach its floor. The previous schema (schemaVersion 1) locked debtSourceCount/categoryCounts to exact values plus a debtSourceSha256 of the joined debt-source list; that exact-match semantics is incompatible with a ratchet (any real decrease changes the hash, which would force a manual baseline edit on every legitimate cleanup -- the same 'edit the number to make it green' anti-pattern the ratchet exists to remove), so debtSourceSha256 has been dropped rather than kept as dead weight. debtSources supersedes it: unlike a hash, it is diffable, human-readable, and (via the per-category subset check) still catches a same-count swap of one tracked debt source for a different, previously-untracked one, which a bare numeric ceiling alone would miss.
